title: MIL-STD-662, V50 Ballistic Test for Armor
organization: U.S. Defense Logistics Agency / Army Research Laboratory
use: Definitions and procedure for ballistic-limit testing of metallic, nonmetallic and composite armor; V50 is a measured test outcome.
limits: V50 is specific to the projectile, test setup, target construction and test definition; not a universal penetration rule.

title: Assessment of Uncertainty in Ballistic Response Estimates Obtained from Ballistic Limit Testing
organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (Riley, Rice, Forster)
use: Explains different perforation-probability curve shapes, V50 uncertainty, dependence on number of shots and test design; useful for estimating run-to-run variation.
limits: Study uses modelled test results and focuses on ballistic limit statistics; it is not a constitutive model for WWII tank plate.

title: The Mechanical Metallurgy of Armour Steels (DST-Group-TR-3305)
organization: Australian Defence Science and Technology Group; S. J. Cimpoeru
use: Armour steel strength, hardness, high-strain-rate behaviour, toughness, adiabatic shear, structural cracking and dual-hardness armour.
limits: General armour-steel reference; modern materials are not identical to captured WWII German plate.

title: German Explosive Ordnance (Projectiles and Projectile Fuzes), TM 9-1985-3
organization: U.S. Army / U.S. Air Force, U.S. Government Printing Office
type: Official technical manual based on captured ordnance documentation
use: Projectile identification, construction diagrams, ammunition variants, fuze and filler details.
limits: Post-war identification manual; verify exact tank-gun variant, manufacturing batch and nomenclature before transferring a record.

title: OP 1666, Volume 2: German Explosive Ordnance
organization: U.S. Navy Bureau of Ordnance
use: Contemporary captured-ammunition descriptions, projectile cross-sections, weights and variant details, including 8.8 cm projectiles.
limits: Large scan; ammunition variants and source-era terminology can differ. Confirm that the entry belongs to KwK/Pak 43 rather than FlaK variants.

title: TM E9-369A: German 88-mm Antiaircraft Gun Materiel
organization: U.S. War Department, Chief of Ordnance
use: Original 8.8 cm FlaK gun/ammunition construction, drawings and firing tables; useful for understanding related projectile families.
limits: FlaK gun variant is not interchangeable in data models with Tiger I KwK 36 or Tiger II KwK 43 simply because calibre matches.

title: 8,8 cm Kw K 36 (L/56)
organization: Panzerworld, Christian Ankerstjerne; references Jentz/Doyle and Pawlas
type: Curated secondary technical table with source bibliography
use: Tiger I gun and ammunition mass, muzzle velocity, and a distance-indexed penetration reference series.
limits: Secondary compilation; the web table does not fully restate the original penetration acceptance criterion, target hardness details, or angular datum. Keep values as a source-specific benchmark series.

title: 8,8 cm Kw K 43 (L/71)
organization: Panzerworld, Christian Ankerstjerne; references Jentz/Doyle, Pawlas and German manuals
type: Curated secondary technical table with source bibliography
use: Tiger II gun, Pzgr 39/43 and Pzgr 40/43 mass/velocity data; published range-indexed values.
limits: Secondary compilation; published penetration curves differ slightly from other transcriptions of wartime tables and must remain separate.

title: OSINT-based analysis of weapon components, optical systems, ammunition, and ballistic performance of the German 8.8 cm FlaK family
organization: Rijad Osmanovic, Faruk Sukurica, Alan Catovic, Defense and Security Studies
type: Peer-reviewed open-access secondary analysis citing primary manuals
use: Transcribes 30°-obliquity Pzgr.39-family curves with a stated 50% perforation definition on RHA HB 275–302 and cites Munitionsmerkblatt 5 and OP 1666.
limits: Secondary transcription; its KwK36/Pak43 numbers differ slightly from Panzerworld series. Original table angle convention and complete method should be checked before high-precision calibration.

title: Germany’s Tiger Tanks: D.W. to Tiger I, Design, Production & Modifications
organization: Thomas L. Jentz and Hilary L. Doyle
type: Historical technical monograph reproducing wartime reports
use: Tiger I armour geometry, captured-vehicle examination and hardness readings; identifies limits of portable Poldi readings.
limits: A secondary book reproducing contemporary documents; individual vehicle and plate data must not be assumed universal for every production year.

title: Germany’s Tiger Tanks: VK45.02 to Tiger II
organization: Thomas L. Jentz and Hilary L. Doyle
type: Historical technical monograph reproducing wartime reports
use: Tiger II production and early turret variants, quoted British Report No.17/Chobham armour measurements, hardness and steel specification records.
limits: The early Turm Nr.1–50 turret steel/specification is not representative of every production turret; field hardness readings are surface measurements.

title: Firing trials in Tunisia against the hull of a Pz.Kw.VI (Tiger), WO 194/744
organization: British Army / War Office; archival report excerpts transcribed by Tank Archives
type: Contemporary British firing-test report, accessed via transcription
use: Shows variable plate response, spalling/flaking and different ballistic-limit behaviour on different areas of a captured Tiger I.
limits: Online article excerpts a report rather than presenting a complete digitized primary report; test projectile and plate details vary by shot.

title: King Tiger Penetration: results of penetration tests of the German Tiger B heavy tank
organization: Soviet 5th Guards Army artillery report, transcribed by Tank Archives; archive ref CAMD RF F.328 Op.4867 D.48 L.133
type: Contemporary test report transcription / archive lead
use: Documents angle-sensitive outcomes: frontal plates not penetrated in stated conditions, one 152 mm hit near MG ball penetrated, and vulnerable running gear.
limits: The article provides summary notes and a scan/archive link; angle wording and the exact impact configuration must be checked against the original before quantitative calibration.

title: Was the Tiger really “King?” Testing the King Tiger at Kubinka
organization: The Russian Battlefield; translated test-report summary
use: Reports cracking, spalling, weld-seam failures, multi-hit damage and plate-to-plate variability on captured Tiger II #502; records non-penetration and penetration observations for different guns and hit locations.
limits: A translated secondary page summarizing Soviet trials; tests are not a controlled ballistic-limit matrix and some ammunition/angle particulars are absent from the excerpt.

title: British examination of captured Tiger II turret; A.F.V.(T) Report No.17, and Preliminary Report on armour quality and vulnerability
organization: British Army technical examination, quoted in Jentz/Doyle
type: Contemporary report reproduced by technical monograph
use: Example production-turret sample readings: 180 mm turret front and 150 mm glacis, with surface Poldi hardness readings; makes production-variant and measurement caveats visible.
limits: Not a complete digitized primary report at this URL; angle notation and hardness instrument limitations must be preserved.

title: U.S. Army 1944 Firing Test No.1: comparative firing program at Shoeburyness
organization: U.S. Army AFV & Weapons Section, memorandum dated 24 May 1944; hosted transcription
use: Documented conditions for 120 mm RHA at 30° obliquity, 100 mm backed by vertical 100 mm plate, and a 20 mm plate spaced 152 mm ahead of 50 mm face-hardened plate; useful for layered target test design.
limits: The report itself says the firing program was too brief for positive conclusions. It is an Allied ammunition/plate experiment, not a Tiger-specific calibration.

title: U.S. Army 1944 Firing Test No.2
organization: U.S. Army Ordnance Board test memorandum, hosted transcription
use: Captured Panther armour and multiple projectile outcomes; helps distinguish armour condition and test normality from generalized penetration claims.
limits: Panther, not Tiger; a transcription; do not re-use its results as Tiger armour values.

title: Metallurgical Examination of a 3-1/4 in. Thick Armor Plate from a German PzKw V (Panther) Tank
organization: Watertown Arsenal Laboratories; NTIS report ADA954952
use: Shows composition, hardness, heat treatment and toughness can coexist in non-intuitive ways; reported Panther sample hardness 262–269 HB with low toughness and susceptibility to shattering.
limits: Panther plate, not Tiger plate; never assign these material properties to Tiger armour. Use as evidence that hardness alone is insufficient.

title: Examination of enemy materiel: metallurgical examination of welded armour plate, German PzKw III tank (OSRD No. 3236 / Progress Report No. M-212)
organization: U.S. Office of Scientific Research and Development / Battelle Memorial Institute
type: Contemporary metallurgical report, Library of Congress catalog
use: Provides a template for the historical examination of chemical composition, hardness survey, physical properties and microstructure.
limits: Panzer III plate; use methodologically, not as Tiger material data.

title: Normal and oblique impact of a kinetic energy projectile on mild steel plates
organization: International Journal of Impact Engineering
use: Experimental results on normal and oblique impact, residual velocity, velocity drop and ricochet for projectiles against 10–25 mm mild steel plates.
limits: 6.2 mm projectile at about 820 m/s against mild steel, not a direct scale analogue for 88 mm APCBC versus thick WWII armour.

title: The penetration of thick steel plates by ogive shaped projectiles—experiment and analysis
organization: International Journal of Impact Engineering
use: Controlled 20 mm ogive projectile tests versus 20, 40 and 80 mm steel plates at 300–800 m/s; data include penetration depth and crater/bulge geometry.
limits: Rigid/non-deforming ogive projectile and normal impact; this is a solver validation benchmark, not the Tiger APCBC model.

title: Oblique perforation of thick metallic plates by rigid projectiles
organization: Xiaowei Chen, Qingming Li, Saucheong Fan; Acta Mechanica Sinica
use: Links nose geometry, target thickness, obliquity, hole enlargement, shear plugging, residual velocity, directional change and ricochet.
limits: Analytical model assumes rigid projectiles in its stated domain; not sufficient on its own for deformable APCBC shells.

title: Oblique impact on single, layered and spaced mild steel targets by 7.62 AP projectiles
organization: International Journal of Impact Engineering
use: Shows plate spacing, layering and obliquity must be modelled as explicit geometry and interaction, not simply added thickness.
limits: Small-calibre projectile and mild steel; mechanistic guidance rather than direct WWII calibration.

title: Johnson–Cook parameter evaluation from ballistic impact data via iterative FEM modelling
organization: Burley, Campbell, Dean and Clyne; University of Cambridge repository
use: Demonstrates calibrating strain-rate-dependent plasticity parameters by comparing simulations with measured impact and residual-indentation outcomes.
limits: Parameter values are material-specific; do not copy one steel’s constants into historical German armour.

title: Modification and experimental validation of the Forrestal–Warren perforation model for high hardness armor steel plates of intermediate thickness
organization: Defence Technology
use: Shows high-hardness armour can fail by adiabatic shear plugging and uses measured residual velocities and plug properties for validation.
limits: ARMOX 500T and API threat; not a direct parameter source for WWII RHA.

title: Model for ballistic fragmentation and behind-armor debris
organization: International Journal of Impact Engineering
use: Addresses chaotic fragmentation, projectile/target fracture and behind-armour debris; useful for secondary fragment outputs.
limits: Model assumptions and parameter calibration needed; does not by itself predict the exact fragments from a specific Tiger plate.

title: The Tank Museum Archive and Object Collection
organization: The Tank Museum, Bovington
evidence_grade: A for provenance, not numerical data
use: Reference collection of technical records, documents, photographs, drawings and objects.
limits: Catalogue/consultation access may be required; a museum object photo alone does not establish material properties.

title: Australian Armour & Artillery Museum exhibits
organization: Australian Armour & Artillery Museum
evidence_grade: A for object identification, not numerical data
use: Australian museum vehicle and artillery collections for reference views and dimensions to cross-check visual assets.
limits: Exhibit labels and photos are not substitutes for factory drawings or ballistic reports.

title: Tiger I frontal turret plate construction and factory drawing references
organization: Tiger1.info technical reference
use: Explains Tiger I turret cheek/front plate construction, openings and local geometry around the gun mantlet.
limits: Specialist secondary page; validate plate geometry against factory drawing or technical manual if precise CAD is required.

title: PzKpfw VI Tiger I and Tiger II armour profile pack
organization: AFV Weapons Profile Pack 48 (scan-hosted reference)
use: Quick cross-check of tank armour locations and geometric conventions.
limits: Secondary profile; do not resolve conflicting angles from this source alone.

title: Armor Penetration Table
organization: Panzerworld, curated historical tables
use: Cross-checks German AP/APCR/HEAT range curves and differentiates guns/round variants.
limits: Tabulated penetration definitions are not fully specified for every row; maintain source identity and uncertainty.

title: Types of ammunition / types of armour
organization: Norfolk Tank Museum
use: Accessible taxonomy and terminology for later game UI labels.
limits: Introductory descriptions only; not simulation parameters.

title: APFSDS Diagram (reference visual)
organization: Wikimedia Commons contributor
evidence_grade: C for engineering detail; usable for visual orientation subject to license
use: Later-era long-rod penetrator and sabot visual decomposition.
limits: Diagram is not a source for material constants or penetration values; check license and attribution on the file page before redistribution.

title: Tank ammunition category image archive
organization: Wikimedia Commons
evidence_grade: C for images; item-level check required
use: Visual references of round shapes and museum displays.
limits: Every file needs its own license/attribution check; images can be miscaptioned.
